title: Warning concerning fraudulent activities by persons misusing the name of Quintet Private Bank (Europe) S.A.
title_original: Warning concerning fraudulent activities by persons misusing the name of Quintet Private Bank (Europe) S.A.
summary: The CSSF warns about fraudulent persons misusing the name of Quintet Private Bank (Europe) S.A. The notice aims to protect the public and customers from impersonation scams and does not create a new prudential obligation for the bank.
why_kept: Luxembourg institutions should monitor and respond to impersonation attempts that may damage their customers, reputation and fraud controls.
actions: Verify suspicious communications, warn customers through appropriate channels, and report suspected fraud to the relevant authorities.

title: Warning concerning fraudulent activities by persons misusing the name of ADEPA ASSET MANAGEMENT S.A.
title_original: Warning concerning fraudulent activities by persons misusing the name of ADEPA ASSET MANAGEMENT S.A.
summary: The CSSF warns about fraudulent persons misusing the name of ADEPA ASSET MANAGEMENT S.A. The notice is intended to prevent investors and the public from being deceived by impersonators and does not impose a new regulatory requirement on ADEPA.
why_kept: Luxembourg investment managers are exposed to client, reputational and fraud risks arising from the misuse of their identity.
actions: Verify suspicious approaches, alert clients and counterparties, and report suspected impersonation or fraud to the authorities.

title: Warning concerning fraudulent activities by persons misusing the name of DAC Investments S.à r.l.
title_original: Warning concerning fraudulent activities by persons misusing the name of DAC Investments S.à r.l.
summary: The CSSF warns about fraudulent persons misusing the name of DAC Investments S.à r.l. The notice seeks to protect the public and potential investors from impersonation scams and does not introduce a new obligation for the named entity.
why_kept: The warning is relevant to Luxembourg firms because impersonation fraud can affect clients, counterparties and institutional reputation.
actions: Verify suspicious communications, notify affected clients or counterparties, and report suspected fraud to the authorities.

title: The EBA responds to the European Commission’s non-adoption of draft amending technical standards on prior permission
title_original: The EBA responds to the European Commission’s non-adoption of draft amending technical standards on prior permission
summary: The EBA comments on the European Commission’s non-adoption of proposed amendments to Delegated Regulation (EU) No 241/2014 that would have shortened the application period for reducing own funds and eligible liabilities instruments. The existing approval framework therefore remains applicable, affecting credit institutions undertaking such reductions and their capital and resolution planning.
why_kept: Luxembourg credit institutions must account for the unchanged prior-permission process when planning capital or eligible-liability reductions.
actions: Review planned reductions of own funds or eligible liabilities, retain sufficient lead time for prior-permission applications, and update capital and resolution plans where necessary.

title: Guidelines on cooperation with the FIU
title_original: Lignes directrices sur la coopération avec la CRF
summary: The Luxembourg FIU's guidelines explain how obliged entities should cooperate with the FIU, including the submission of suspicious transaction reports, responses to FIU information requests and compliance with orders. They provide practical expectations for AML/CFT reporting and cooperation in Luxembourg.
why_kept: Luxembourg financial institutions subject to AML/CFT obligations must align their FIU reporting and cooperation procedures with these national expectations.
actions: Review and update FIU cooperation procedures, SAR/STR workflows, response processes and relevant staff training.

title: Crypto-Asset Misuse in Financial Crime: Strategic Findings and Typologies
title_original: Crypto-Asset Misuse in Financial Crime: Strategic Findings and Typologies
summary: This strategic analysis examines the evolution of crypto-asset misuse in financial crime, including methodologies, findings and typologies relevant to money laundering and terrorist financing. It is an analytical and awareness document rather than a binding rule, but it informs risk assessment and detection practices for reporting entities exposed to crypto-assets.
why_kept: Luxembourg institutions with crypto-asset exposure or crypto-asset counterparties can use the typologies to improve financial-crime risk assessments and monitoring.
actions: Assess the typologies against the institution's risk profile and update transaction-monitoring scenarios, CDD/EDD measures and staff awareness where appropriate.

title: AMLA launches a consultation on a new EU suspicious transaction report format
title_original: L'AMLA lance une consultation sur un nouveau format de déclaration de soupçon dans l'UE
summary: AMLA is consulting on a harmonised format for suspicious transaction reports in the EU. The initiative is intended to improve consistency and effectiveness in the collection and exchange of AML/CFT information and may affect the reporting processes and systems of obliged financial entities across the EU.
why_kept: A future EU-wide STR format could require Luxembourg institutions to modify reporting data, controls and technical interfaces with the FIU.
actions: Review the consultation, assess operational and data impacts, submit feedback if relevant and prepare to map existing STR processes to the proposed format.

title: Reporting of typologies and relevant information presenting a significant fraud risk (Bill No. 8722)
title_original: Signalement des typologies et informations pertinentes présentant un risque important de fraude (PDL N°8722)
summary: This Luxembourg publication concerns the reporting of fraud-related typologies and other relevant information presenting a significant fraud risk in the context of Bill No. 8722. It is relevant to reporting entities because it may shape expectations for identifying, documenting and communicating fraud indicators to competent authorities.
why_kept: Luxembourg financial institutions should monitor the bill and the FIU's fraud-risk expectations when reviewing AML/CFT and fraud-reporting controls.
actions: Review the proposed requirements and fraud typologies, assess reporting and escalation procedures, and prepare control changes if the bill is adopted.

title: Update to goAML indicators
title_original: Mise à jour des indicateurs goAML
summary: The Luxembourg FIU has updated the indicator framework available in the goAML system, which now contains twelve categories of indicators. The indicators are intended to help reporting entities structure and improve suspicious transaction reporting.
why_kept: Luxembourg reporting entities using goAML may need to reflect the revised indicators in their alert assessment and SAR/STR preparation processes.
actions: Review the revised indicator categories, update relevant procedures and monitoring or case-management configurations, and brief staff responsible for SAR/STR filing.

title: goAML FAQ
title_original: goAML FAQ
summary: The Luxembourg FIU has moved its goAML frequently asked questions to its main website. The FAQ provides practical clarification for reporting entities using goAML and preparing or submitting AML/CFT reports.
why_kept: Luxembourg institutions filing through goAML can use the centralised FAQ to resolve reporting and system-use questions.
actions: Check the relocated FAQ when submitting reports and update internal links or guidance to point to the new location.

title: Bribery of Foreign Public Officials (BFPO)
title_original: Bribery of Foreign Public Officials (BFPO)
summary: This Luxembourg guidance paper raises awareness of bribery of foreign public officials and provides practical guidance for reporting entities on detecting such cases. It supports AML/CFT controls concerning corruption proceeds, politically exposed persons and suspicious transaction reporting.
why_kept: Corruption-related proceeds can create material AML, reputational and regulatory risks for Luxembourg financial institutions and their clients.
actions: Review corruption and PEP risk controls, enhance relevant CDD/EDD and transaction-monitoring scenarios, train staff and report suspicions where required.

title: New Article 506-1 of the Criminal Code
title_original: Nouvel article 506-1 du Code Pénal
summary: The Luxembourg Law of 12 December 2025 amended Article 506-1 of the Criminal Code by replacing the former list of predicate offences with a general reference to all crimes and misdemeanours. This broadens and clarifies the criminal-law basis relevant to money-laundering risk and may affect the assessment and reporting of suspicious activity.
why_kept: The broader predicate-offence scope is relevant to Luxembourg institutions' AML risk assessments, transaction monitoring and suspicious-activity escalation.
actions: Assess the impact on AML risk taxonomies, monitoring scenarios, investigations and SAR/STR escalation criteria, and update legal references in relevant policies.

title: 2024 Annual Report
title_original: 2024 Rapport Annuel
summary: The Luxembourg FIU's 23rd annual report covers its activities during 2024 and describes continuing efforts to combat money laundering and terrorist financing. It is a retrospective institutional and statistical publication that may provide market-wide trends and supervisory context, but does not itself impose new obligations.
why_kept: The report gives Luxembourg financial institutions useful insight into FIU activity, reporting trends and emerging AML/CFT risk areas.

title: Publication of the goAML indicators brochure (part 1)
title_original: Publication de la brochure sur les indicateurs goAML (partie 1)
summary: The Luxembourg FIU has published a manual describing new structured goAML indicators to help reporting entities prepare suspicious activity reports. The brochure supports more consistent identification, classification and communication of AML/CFT suspicions through the goAML system.
why_kept: The indicators can affect how Luxembourg institutions document alerts and prepare SAR/STR filings in goAML.
actions: Review the manual, map the indicators to internal typologies and case-management processes, and train relevant AML and reporting staff.

title: Business Mail Compromise targeting the investment sector
title_original: Business Mail Compromise targeting the investment sector
summary: The Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit reports an increase in business email compromise and related cyber fraud targeting investment-sector professionals. The alert is intended to raise awareness and prompt firms to strengthen vigilance over payment instructions, communications and suspicious activity.
why_kept: Luxembourg investment firms and PSF may be targeted and should consider the alert in their financial-crime and cybersecurity controls.
actions: Review business email compromise controls, verify payment and account-change requests through independent channels, reinforce staff awareness and assess whether incidents require internal escalation or suspicious-transaction reporting.

title: Frank Elderson: Fireside chat
title_original: Frank Elderson: Fireside chat
summary: A fireside chat with Frank Elderson, a member of the ECB Executive Board and the ECB’s supervisory leadership, concerning banking supervision. No specific binding measure, framework or compliance deadline is identified in the supplied information.
why_kept: ECB/SSM communications can signal supervisory priorities relevant to Luxembourg credit institutions supervised within the SSM.
actions: Review the full discussion for supervisory expectations or emerging priorities and consider whether they require updates to the institution’s supervisory engagement or control framework.

title: Warning concerning fraudulent activities by persons misusing the name of TEIKO ASSET MANAGEMENT S.À R.L.
title_original: Warning concerning fraudulent activities by persons misusing the name of TEIKO ASSET MANAGEMENT S.À R.L.
summary: The CSSF warns the public about persons conducting fraudulent activities while misusing the name of TEIKO ASSET MANAGEMENT S.À R.L. The notice is aimed at preventing investors and counterparties from dealing with unauthorised or fraudulent actors and does not impose a new obligation on the named firm.
why_kept: Luxembourg financial institutions should be able to identify and escalate impersonation and fraud attempts involving regulated firms.
actions: Circulate the warning to relevant compliance, fraud and client-facing teams; verify purported communications involving the firm; and report suspected fraud to the CSSF or competent authorities.

title: OPSG advice - Combined Stakeholder Pensions Report - EIOPA 2026 Consumer Trends Process
title_original: OPSG advice - Combined Stakeholder Pensions Report - EIOPA 2026 Consumer Trends Process
summary: The EIOPA Occupational Pensions Stakeholder Group provides advice in the context of EIOPA’s 2026 consumer-trends process and its combined stakeholder pensions report. It informs EIOPA’s assessment of consumer and member trends in the pensions sector rather than introducing directly binding requirements.
why_kept: Luxembourg pension funds and related institutions may be affected by future supervisory priorities or consumer-protection measures arising from EIOPA’s findings.
actions: Review the advice for emerging consumer-protection and pension-member risks and consider whether governance, disclosure or conduct practices require adjustment.

title: Opinion on the amendments to buy-back programmes and stabilisation measures
title_original: Opinion on the amendments to buy-back programmes and stabilisation measures
summary: ESMA issues an opinion on amendments concerning buy-back programmes and stabilisation measures under the Market Abuse Regulation. The opinion contributes to the EU legislative or technical review of the applicable framework for issuers and market participants but is not itself directly binding.
why_kept: Luxembourg issuers and firms involved in securities transactions should anticipate changes to the conditions, controls and documentation surrounding buy-backs and stabilisation.
actions: Review the opinion against existing buy-back and stabilisation procedures, monitor the subsequent EU legislative process, and prepare to update controls, disclosures and records if amendments are adopted.

title: Publication of Study Cahier 210 - Bank Lending in the Euro Area: The Role of Bank-Firm Switching and Market Concentration
title_original: Publication du Cahier d'études 210 - Bank Lending in the Euro Area: The Role of Bank-Firm Switching and Market Concentration
summary: This BCL study analyses how lending conditions change when non-financial companies switch banks, using AnaCredit data covering more than seven million loans granted by over 2,000 euro-area banks between January 2021 and June 2025. It provides research on bank-firm relationships and market concentration rather than introducing binding requirements.
why_kept: The findings may inform Luxembourg banks’ assessments of credit-market structure, borrower relationships and concentration risk.

title: CSSF-ALFI webinar on valuation
title_original: CSSF-ALFI webinar on valuation
summary: This notice concerns a CSSF-ALFI webinar addressing valuation matters relevant to investment fund managers. It is an information and engagement event rather than a binding regulatory instrument.
why_kept: Valuation remains a key supervisory and control area for Luxembourg investment fund managers.

title: ESMA signs Memorandum of Understanding with the Securities and Exchange Board of India
title_original: ESMA signs Memorandum of Understanding with the Securities and Exchange Board of India
summary: ESMA has signed an MoU with India’s SEBI to facilitate supervisory cooperation and information exchange concerning the recognition of Indian central counterparties. The arrangement supports the EU framework for third-country CCP access and cross-border clearing, but does not itself create direct obligations for ordinary Luxembourg financial institutions.
why_kept: Luxembourg firms using or interacting with third-country CCPs may be affected by the availability and conditions of EU recognition.

title: Memorandum of Understanding between ESMA and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on central counterparties
title_original: Memorandum of Understanding between ESMA and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on central counterparties
summary: This MoU establishes cooperation and information-sharing arrangements between ESMA and SEBI regarding central counterparties established in India and supervised by SEBI. It supports the supervisory basis for possible EU recognition of Indian CCPs under the EU third-country framework.
why_kept: The arrangement may affect access to and oversight of Indian CCPs used by Luxembourg and other EU market participants.

title: Launch of Luxembourg Future Fund 3
title_original: Lancement du Luxembourg Future Fund 3
summary: The Luxembourg authorities, SNCI and the European Investment Fund announced the launch of Luxembourg Future Fund 3, a public investment initiative. The announcement concerns financing and investment activity in Luxembourg rather than a new regulatory requirement.
why_kept: The initiative may create investment, co-investment and financing opportunities relevant to Luxembourg financial-sector participants.

title: Global situation of undertakings for collective investment at the end of July 2026
title_original: Global situation of undertakings for collective investment at the end of July 2026
summary: This CSSF press release presents the aggregate situation of Luxembourg undertakings for collective investment at the end of July 2026. It is a statistical and market-monitoring publication covering the investment-fund sector and does not introduce new compliance obligations.
why_kept: The figures provide Luxembourg fund managers and other market participants with current information on the size and condition of the domestic investment-fund sector.

title: Klaus Löber's speech at the PostTrade 360°, 2 September 2026
title_original: Klaus Löber's speech at the PostTrade 360°, 2 September 2026
summary: An ESMA speech addressing central counterparty and post-trade topics. It is informational rather than a binding measure, but may indicate ESMA’s supervisory priorities for EU clearing markets.
why_kept: Luxembourg firms participating in clearing or relying on EU post-trade infrastructures may need to monitor the supervisory direction signalled by ESMA.
actions: Review the speech for relevant supervisory expectations and assess whether any clearing or post-trade policies require updating.
